messages:
maya: Heads-up — running into weird quota attribution when a request carries both project and service-account claims. Console shows project usage but billing shows SA bucket. Is this by design?

own: We designed it to prefer the lowest-level principal (SA) for chargeback, but routing uses 'origin' to decide quotas. Can you paste an example request?

maya: Sure — header we emit from client:```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.com
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
X-Org: org-123
X-Project: proj-987
X-Service-Account: sa-42
```

tess: If SA present, authz resolves to SA for effective identity. But quota layers are: project quotas -> org quotas -> sa-specific limits. We should only charge SA if SA has an explicit billing account attached.

maya: In this case SA has no billing account (it's project-owned); console still shows project meter but the billing export shows SA labels.

raj: That sounds like a label propagation bug in the ingestion pipeline. The routing decision path and the billing label emission are two different codepaths. We probably map effective_identity in routing, but the metrics emitter uses raw token claims.

maya: Right — could that cause double-counting in dashboards?

own: Potentially. Dashboard aggregates are keyed by label sets; if two services use different keys (project vs sa) the dashboard would split, while billing export attaches both and downstream join ends up attributing to SA.

infra-bot: Canary deploy succeeded: authz-service v2.4.1 -> canary on cluster-a (12:05 UTC).

tess: Quick proposal: normalize effective identity at the authz edge and add a single canonical label 'effective_principal' that downstream systems must use. Backwards compatible if we also emit legacy labels for 30 days.

raj: Agree. Also need rule for when SA should override project: if SA has explicit billing_account then SA wins; else project wins. Add a triage: SA_has_billing -> SA, else Project.

mia: UX ask — console people expect the logs/usage page to show "who paid" vs "who executed" separately. Can we add two columns: executor (effective principal) and billed_to (billing principal)?

own: That seems reasonable. executor -> routing identity; billed_to -> decided by billing policy. Implementable with the canonical labels.

maya: Timeline? This bug is causing confusion for one customer on Dedicated. They reported unexpected invoices.

tess: I'll cut a small PR to authz to set effective_principal label + update metrics emitter to use it. Then update billing pipeline to prefer billed_to rule. Target: patch + canary tomorrow.

raj: I'll add e2e test to ensure console and billing exports converge on billed_to for same request. Also add a quick migration script to reprocess last 7 days of events for that customer.

mia: I'll draft a small console note explaining the two columns and the policy rules, and we can surface the migration for affected orgs.

maya: Thanks — appreciate fast turnaround. One more: can we include request path in the help doc so support can correlate traces?

infra-bot: Trace link: https://traces.internal.redwood/trace/abc123 (sample).

own: Good catch. Let's keep this thread for status. I'll drop PR links once created. :thumbsup:

maya: Ack. Will loop in account team after migration plan is ready.
